source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus declares 116 megawatts of IT capacity across three buildings, the second-largest published power figure among Virginia data centers.

That 116 megawatts is a declared IT capacity figure, not a measurement of actual draw. The campus covers 1,177,019 square feet of technical space across facilities NVA5, NVA6, and NVA7. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the declared capacity could support roughly 2,900 racks of accelerators. The operator's specifications do not state what equipment is installed or how much of the capacity is in use.

Virginia publishes IT capacity for only 25 of the 330 data center facilities mapped in the state, totaling 1,603 megawatts. Sterling alone accounts for 7.2 percent of that declared total. For AI scaling the binding question is how much power a site can deliver to accelerators, and this is one of the few Virginia sites where that number is published rather than inferred. The concentration is the point: one campus in one city holds a measurable share of everything the state has disclosed.

What the data does not cover is as large as what it does. No certifications are listed for the campus. The specifications omit total power draw, PUE, cooling technology, and grid interconnection details. Nothing states whether the site is constrained by power supply or grid availability in Northern Virginia. The suitability score of 80 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing, so the data cannot show whether this campus is growing.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
